FINMO.A2: Three-statement financial model. All formulas reference Model Inputs and in-sheet statement rows.
FINMO.A81: Cash as Months of Operating Cost
FINMO.B64: Payroll + Lease/Rent + Depreciation + Interest (owner compensation is inside payroll)

FINMO.B68: HEADLINE - pre-tax accounting: Fixed Costs / Contribution Margin (0 = unreachable)
FINMO.B69: (Payroll + Lease + Interest + scheduled principal) / Contribution Margin

Valuation.A17: Cost of capital — a build-up, applied the same way for every business
Valuation.A2: Discounted cash flow built from this model's own figures. Every input below is labelled GROUNDED or ASSUMPTION with its source.
Valuation.A37: Terminal value — both methods, side by side
Valuation.A4: Inputs — what is grounded and what is assumed
Valuation.A40: Terminal value used (average of the two)
Valuation.A44: Present value of forecast cash flows
Valuation.A50: Sensitivity — the range is the answer, not the single number
Valuation.A51: Equity value at WACC (down) x terminal growth (across)
Valuation.A59: How to read this: the cash flows, tax rate, cost of debt and capital weights come from this model. The risk-free rate is the 10-year US Treasury. The equity risk premium, size and company-specific premiums, terminal growth rate and exit multiple are assumptions - each is shown above with the source it came from and the date that figure was published, and each is an amber cell you can change. A valuation of a private business is a range, not a number; the grid above shows how the answer moves when the two assumptions it is most sensitive to move.
Valuation.A61: Seller's discretionary earnings (SDE) adds the owner's pay back to EBITDA, because a buyer of an owner-operated business acquires that role too - and the transaction multiples above are quoted against SDE.
Valuation.C18: risk-free + equity risk premium + size premium + company-specific premium
Valuation.C19: book weights from the Year 1 balance sheet
Valuation.C21: cost of equity and after-tax cost of debt, weighted
Valuation.C22: the perpetuity method is only shown when this clears the 3-point floor
Valuation.C38: last year's free cash flow grown forever, discounted at WACC less growth; shown only when the spread clears the floor
Valuation.C39: year-5 seller's discretionary earnings at the multiple businesses of this kind actually transact at
Valuation.C40: neither method is authoritative; the sensitivity grid below is the honest answer
Valuation.C46: debt less cash on the opening balance sheet. Negative means the business already holds more cash than debt, which adds to value
Valuation.C48: the cross-check: if this sits far from the exit multiple above, the two methods disagree
Valuation.D14: The model's own effective tax rate
Valuation.D15: SBA 7(a) median rate for this industry and state, carried by the model
